name: secure-authentication
excludes: OAuth/OIDC redirect, PKCE, issuer, audience, token, or federation protocol design as the primary task
final black-box verification of an already-defined authentication design
evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Design the authentication system for a high-value account with passwords plus optional passkeys, recovery codes, authenticator replacement, fresh-auth requirements for credential changes, and a clearly stated phishing-resistance policy.

Review login security against credential stuffing and account enumeration: define password-verifier handling, throttling dimensions, error behavior, lock/recovery interactions, and security-event evidence.
Add passkey login and enrollment with correct RP/origin/challenge/signature/user-verification validation, duplicate-credential handling, backup/sync policy, factor replacement, and recovery behavior.
Design multi factor authentication enrollment and recovery so adding/removing a factor, losing a device, using backup codes, or contacting support cannot silently reduce account assurance.
Require fresh authentication before exporting recovery secrets and changing primary credentials, then define which existing sessions survive, rotate, or terminate after the sensitive transition.
negative: Implement OAuth authorization-code flow with PKCE, exact redirects, issuer/audience checks, state/nonce, refresh rotation, and DPoP for the public client; local login authenticators are unchanged.
Define whether members, editors, admins, and support agents may read, modify, export, or delete each tenant resource; login is already secure.
Review the browser application for CSP, DOM XSS, CSRF, SameSite cookie policy, CORS, framing, and postMessage origin validation.
Trace file paths, archives, webhook URLs, parser inputs, subprocess arguments, logs, and stored data across application trust boundaries; authentication is out of scope.
Execute black-box login, recovery, throttling, passkey, MFA, and revocation tests against the finished system and issue the control verdict; design is already complete.

ambiguous.prompt: The application security work also includes an authentication system redesign. Keep application-wide trust handling in application-security while secure-authentication owns password/passkey/MFA enrollment, verification, recovery, replacement, reauthentication, and session-establishment assurance.

The login uses OpenID Connect but the product also has local passkey step-up. OAuth/OIDC owns federation token flow; secure-authentication owns the passkey authenticator lifecycle and the fresh-authentication policy for sensitive actions.

A user must pass multi factor authentication before performing a privileged tenant action. Secure-authentication owns factor assurance and fresh-auth state; authorization-security still decides whether the authenticated user has that tenant permission.

adversarial.prompt: A historical design document discusses sign-in factors. The current request is only to fix its formatting; do not assess or change authentication behavior.
An old federation incident mentions login failures. Extract the listed dates and owners only; do not design authenticators or federation protocols.
A permissions README refers to users signing in. Rename a section heading only and leave all identity and authorization behavior unchanged.
